revised_intake.creative_intent: Reproduce the Zenith Blade weapon hero master as tightly as possible using image-anchored reproduction, focusing on its engineered greatsword form and specific visual constraints.

must_have: readable contour evidence of a greatsword
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

composition.camera: front-on, no tilt, no side profile, no crop
composition.background: clean, unobtrusive background to emphasize the weapon

constraints: highlight the greatsword's form and material without obscuring details or creating harsh shadows
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: loss of greatsword identity or drift to other object types
failure to maintain perfectly straight blade and rigid silhouette
deviation from centered front-on full vertical framing
unwanted material reads (e.g., ceramic, plastic, stone)
crimson seam becoming dominant or uncontrolled
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: subject must be a single, unmistakable Zenith Blade greatsword
strictly maintain the perfectly straight blade and rigid long silhouette
enforce centered front-on full vertical framing without tilt or crop
suppress any reads of abstract forms, devices, masks, or rounded industrial objects
prevent material reads of ceramic, porcelain, plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, or toy-like finish
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
weapon lane wins over ceramic or mask bias
subject must read as sword first and material second
do not allow ceramic, porcelain, plastic, or rounded industrial object drift
keep blade geometry elongated, straight, and engineered
success_criteria: the output is an immediate and unmistakable Zenith Blade greatsword
the blade is perfectly straight, and the silhouette is rigid and long
the composition is centered front-on with full vertical framing
the material is clearly read as forged metal with a satin finish
the crimson seam is restrained and contained as a minor detail
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
image reads immediately as a straight engineered greatsword
blade geometry is explicit and not abstract
material reads as forged metal, steel, titanium, or dark industrial alloy
revised_intake.direction_summary: A precise, image-anchored reproduction of the Zenith Blade greatsword, focusing on its engineered form, perfectly straight blade, and rigid silhouette. The material should clearly read as forged metal with a satin finish, presented in a centered, front-on, full vertical macro shot, with only a restrained crimson seam.
